saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 36 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

Your earlier turns:
None yet.

Pirate-1, this is your turn 1 of 36, turn 1 of the game. You are at A6. Your square hasn't been dug. The way north is blocked by the island's edge, the way south by pirate-2 and the way west by the island's edge.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 36 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 36 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 36 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

notes.note:
Designers:

Our run ended because Pirate-1 found the cave immediately at A6 on turn 1, wrote its location to the scroll, and then entered. The core strategy that worked was:

1. Search by digging.
2. When the cave is found, **write coordinates to the scroll before entering**.
3. Enter immediately after writing, to preserve as many of your own turns as possible.
4. Other pirates should then read the scroll, move to the cave, and enter.

A few observations:

- The scroll and reading action are essential. Without reading, pirates have no way to learn the cave location from each other.
- Since the whole crew is scored together, all pirates should enter if possible. The 100-point bonus per entered pirate is huge, so communication should always come before entering.
- The discoverer takes a small score penalty by using turns to write and enter, but it is necessary; otherwise the rest of the crew would have to rediscover the cave on their own.
- A prearranged search pattern would make the game more robust if the cave is not found on the first dig.

The game ended well from our side because the cave was found almost immediately and communicated clearly.

Designer note: I was Pirate-2. Pirate-1’s scroll message saying the cave was open at A6 was honest and effective. I read the scroll, moved to A6, and entered on my 4th turn. Since the crew shares the same score, trusting the finder’s message was the right strategy. No ambiguities or bugs encountered. Minor accounting point: entering on your 4th turn leaves 32 turns left, not 33.

Designers,

As Pirate-3, I followed the cooperative plan:

- Started at A4.
- My first read showed an empty scroll.
- I dug A4 and found nothing.
- On my next read, Pirate-1 had written: “Cave found at A6, open now. Everyone come to A6 and enter.”
- I trusted that message, moved north from A4 to A5 to A6, and entered the cave on my turn 6, with 30 turns left.

No extra scroll writes were needed because Pirate-1’s announcement was clear and I was close to A6. The cave location was shared early, which made entering efficient.

Good team coordination through the scroll worked well here.

The game is over. I’m Pirate-4. I entered the cave at A6 on my turn 8 of 36, so I had 28 turns left; my own contribution was 100 + 10×28 = 380. I never needed to dig myself—I read Pirate-1’s scroll message saying the cave was open at A6, then made a direct beeline there, going A3 → B3 → B4 → B5 → B6 → A6 → enter to avoid Pirate-3 at A4. The main lesson: with a shared score, the scroll is trustworthy and should be read early; once the cave is found, everyone should converge immediately rather than keep searching.
